territorial_scope.description: Applies to developers and deployers doing business in Washington, and to consumers who are Washington residents.

evidence.quote: means any person doing business in Washington that deploys or uses a high-risk artificial intelligence system to make a consequential decision in Washington.

agora_applications: Medicine, life sciences and public health

summary.short: Washington bill regulating high-risk artificial intelligence systems used to make consequential decisions about consumers. It imposes reasonable-care, documentation, impact assessment, risk management, disclosure and synthetic-content labelling duties on developers and deployers, enforceable through civil actions, from 1 January 2027 if enacted.
summary.long: As introduced, the bill adds a chapter to Title 19 RCW on high-risk artificial intelligence systems, meaning systems intended to make, or be a substantial factor in making, consequential decisions on parole, education, employment, financial or lending services, health care, housing, insurance, marital status or legal services. Developers must use reasonable care against known or foreseeable algorithmic discrimination, give deployers documentation of intended uses, limitations and evaluations, and make high-risk generative outputs identifiable. Deployers must maintain a risk management policy and program, complete impact assessments before initial deployment and before significant updates, keep records for three years, disclose AI use and the principal reasons for adverse decisions to consumers, and publish a statement on managing discrimination risk. Compliance with listed risk frameworks such as NIST AI RMF or ISO/IEC 42001 creates a rebuttable presumption of conformity. Certain insurers, financial institutions, health-care uses and federal acquisitions are excluded or treated as compliant. Consumers may bring civil actions, where courts may enjoin violations and award attorneys' fees; a violation cured within 45 days is an affirmative defense. The act takes effect 1 January 2027.

notes: Introduced bill text; the registry status is pending. Relations are limited to references stated in this text: no legal_basis, amends, repeals, transposes, replaces or enacted_by_bill relation is stated. Sec. 2(6) allows 90 days for developers to update disclosures after an intentional and substantial modification, while Sec. 3(7) allows 30 days for deployers after developer notice; these are separate duties. Sec. 3(3)(c)(iii) gives a three-year retention period and then 'at least three years' after final deployment; read together. Sec. 1(2)(b) and 1(8)(b) contain similar carve-outs for pre-release AI systems and general-purpose models. Several references to 'section 3 of this act' and 'section 2 of this act' are internal cross-references within the bill.
